title: Weather and light timeline for the Battle Theatre, Jun 25 - Jul 5, 1863 (and Nov 19, 1863)
status: PDF-derived and cross-checked against data-src/environment/weather_by_day.json. Secondary-source weather: Jacobs's original sheets were not read (PDF B.10.7). Nothing here is a default; see pdf_recommended_render (PENDING OWNER).
clock: local mean time (LMT); times here are LMT unless a field says otherwise

weak_source_flags: All Jacobs temperature and sky values arrive through secondary summaries (Strategypage/Nofi, Emerging Civil War, TeachersFirst, AMS, HistoryNet, Coastal Point); the original table was not read.
Humidity, dew point, pressure and visibility are open gaps; heat-index figures are estimates by Nese and Harding from Harrisburg observers 35 miles away.
Cloud effects on lux are inferred, not measured. Fog placement is inferred. Dust is inferred.
Timeline rows are seeded_unverified until checked against a primary source (the project Law).

by_day.1863-07-02: Afternoon 'mizzling' per Strategypage versus clearing per Boston Globe; both carried. Rendered as brief light drizzle possible at midday, clearing late afternoon

by_day.1863-07-03: Very gentle S to SSW; no breeze during the Charge

conflicts_carried_as_ranges.pdf_handling: Render a wet showery all day with the heaviest rain from afternoon to night. The timing stays a range.

candidates.statement: Jul 1 to 3 were slightly below average

conflicts_carried_as_ranges.pdf_handling: Inferred resolution: Jul 1 (76 F) and Jul 2 (81 F) were below early-July norms, and Jul 3 at 87 F in shade was near the modern normal highs (modern normals are not 1863 normals). Heat felt worse because of humidity, wool, sun and exertion. Use 87 F shade and a heat index of about 100 F for the Charge.
